title: Tashkent Rising Again
premise: Dominic Lockridge, a private security contractor who specializes in deniable work, receives a call on a burner phone that was supposedly destroyed years ago — and the voice belongs to Mara Voss, his former handler who died in Tashkent three years ago. She claims to be alive, embedded as the personal security chief for a Central Asian oligarch, and offers Dominic a contract: extract her brother-in-arms, a defector carrying proof that Dominic's own agency sold out its assets. As Dominic fights through checkpoints, betrayals, and old debts across Tashkent's underworld, they discover the defector is bait in a trap set by their current employer to flush out Mara — and that Dominic themselves is the real target. In the end, Dominic chooses truth over loyalty, exposing the agency's rot at the cost of their own identity, while Mara vanishes once more, leaving Dominic alive but unrecognizable to everyone they were.
about_author: Lior Nakamura is a former logistics analyst who spent a decade shuttling between Almaty and Istanbul before turning to fiction. They write lean, atmospheric thrillers about people whose jobs require them to have no names.

chapters.title: The Number That Shouldn't Ring
chapters.summary: Dominic Lockridge, mid-contract protecting a nervous banker in Vienna, answers a burner phone they personally destroyed three years ago. The voice is Mara Voss — dead since Tashkent. She gives him forty-eight hours and a name: Arman Bek. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: cold dread cracking open an old grief.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Dominic runs background on Bek, a defector hiding in Tashkent with encrypted drives allegedly proving the Meridian Group sold its own contractors. Dominic's employer, Calloway, assigns them to 'retrieve' Bek — the same job Mara offered. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: the vertigo of realizing two enemies want the same thing.

chapters.title: Chorsu at Midnight
chapters.summary: In Tashkent's bazaar district, Dominic makes contact with Bek through a fixer named Dilnoza, navigating market stalls thick with watchers. Bek is terrified, half-ready to bolt, insisting someone inside Meridian tipped off his location. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: wary trust forming under pressure.

chapters.title: What Mara Left Behind
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter: three years ago, Dominic watched Mara's safehouse burn in Tashkent and identified the body. Now, searching her old dead-drop, Dominic finds evidence the body was staged — by whom? POV: alternating Dominic present-tense and past-tense memory. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion of everyone, including Mara.

chapters.title: The Oligarch's House
chapters.summary: Dominic infiltrates a reception at oligarch Rustam Karimov's compound, where Mara Voss stands openly as head of security — alive, polished, and pretending not to know him. A coded exchange in the wine cellar reveals she's playing a long game against Karimov himself. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: relief poisoned by doubt about which side she's truly on.

chapters.title: Calloway's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dilnoza cracks a fragment of Bek's drives: Meridian has been running false-flag extractions, burning contractors like Dominic to bury evidence. Calloway knew. The extraction contract is a leash. POV: Dilnoza, then Dominic. Emotional beat: betrayal landing like a physical blow; loyalty beginning to invert.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Samarkand Highway
chapters.summary: The extraction goes wrong on the road south: a convoy ambush kills two of Dominic's team, and Bek is taken — but deliberately left alive, a message. Mara appears in the smoke, saving Dominic's life, and admits she used Bek as bait to draw out Meridian's cleaner. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: fury, confession, and the first honest moment between them in years.

chapters.title: The Cleaner
chapters.summary: Meridian's fixer, a ghost from Dominic's own training days known only as Sable, offers Dominic a deal: deliver Mara, keep their name, their pension, their life. Dominic stalls, buying time while Dilnoza moves Bek's drives to a journalist network. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: temptation laid bare — power offered in exchange for complicity.

chapters.title: Tashkent Rising
chapters.summary: Climax. During a citywide blackout engineered by Karimov's rivals, Dominic and Mara assault the compound where Bek is held, facing Sable in a brutal close-quarters fight. Dominic chooses truth over loyalty, broadcasting fragments of the drives live rather than trading them for safety. Sable falls; Karimov's empire begins to crack publicly. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: decisive sacrifice — identity burned as fuel.

chapters.title: Nobody's Name
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the Meridian scandal breaks; Calloway is subpoenaed, and 'Dominic Lockridge' officially dies in a car fire. Living quietly in Almaty under a new name, Dominic receives one last burner call — Mara, alive, free, saying only 'thank you' before the line goes dead. POV: Dominic. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace built on the ruins of an old self.
